jobs.description:
About Sisu

Sisu is a founder-friendly venture studio that partners with early-stage companies from inception through initial scale. We work at the earliest stages—often before incorporation—to help validate ideas, build founding teams, develop MVPs, and prepare companies for fundraising.

Founded by Ari Mir, a serial entrepreneur with more than 20 years of experience, Sisu has helped launch and scale multiple venture-backed companies. Ari has built businesses generating over $100M in annual revenue and employing more than 1,000 people globally.

https://www.sisu.site/

The Role

Sisu is hiring a Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
to lead the technical vision and execution of a new venture developed within our studio. This is a full-time executive leadership role
responsible for designing, building, and scaling the core technology platform of a new company.

The CTO will partner closely with Sisu to define the technical roadmap, build early product infrastructure, and lead engineering execution from initial MVP through early growth. Upon successful formation of the company, the CTO will transition into the Chief Technology Officer role of the newly formed venture.

This role is ideal for a technologist who wants full ownership of technical strategy and architecture while building a company from the ground up.

Key Responsibilities

Define and own the technical architecture, systems design, and engineering roadmap
Lead development of the MVP and iterate toward product-market fit
Make foundational decisions around infrastructure, tooling, and scalability
Hire, mentor, and manage early engineering talent as the company grows
Partner with the CEO on product strategy, roadmap prioritization, and execution
Support investor readiness through technical diligence and roadmap planning

About You (Technical Focus)

We are looking for a top-tier engineer-
an individual who is prepared to go all in on building a disruptive venture from the ground up. You thrive in deeply technical environments that demand relentless ambition and unwavering determination. Sisu’s program is highly selective, admitting only 20 founders a year.

Deep Technical Expertise
: You excel in software architecture, systems design, product development, or related fields. Whether you’re a world-class engineer, a machine learning expert, or a cutting-edge product builder, your capabilities place you in a league of your own.
Entrepreneurial Drive
: You see opportunity where others see risk. You’re actively seeking the right partnership, network, and guidance to bring groundbreaking products to market.
Collaborative Edge
: While you’re fiercely self-driven, you understand the value of working alongside advisors, co-founders, and peers who challenge your thinking. You recognize the advantage of having direct access to a seasoned entrepreneur who’s scaled companies before.

If you see yourself in these qualities, we want to meet you. We’ll provide the tools, mentorship, and resources to build something truly extraordinary.

Application Process

Initial Screening
: A 30-minute phone/video interview with a talent principal.
Founder Interview
: A 30-minute phone/video interview with Ari Mir.
Working Sessions
: Upon acceptance, you’ll join a 24 month program where you’ll work directly with Ari and the Sisu team.

If you’re ready to take the first step, we’d love to hear from you.

Seeking an exceptional Chief Technology Officer / Co-Founder
to help build a vertically integrated artificial intelligence company spanning machine learning, high-performance computing, advanced systems engineering, and ultimately custom compute hardware.

Important: this is an early-stage co-founder position and is unpaid at the outset. Compensation will initially be equity-based, with cash compensation expected only as the company reaches appropriate financing or revenue milestones. Candidates should approach this as a genuine founding commitment, not a conventional salaried executive role.

This is not a conventional software-startup CTO role
. The position requires a deeply hands-on technical founder capable of working across the computing stack—from AI models and distributed systems through GPU infrastructure, compilers, accelerator architecture, semiconductor technology, and physical hardware.

The CTO will be expected to architect, prototype, code, benchmark, debug, research, experiment, and build.

Exceptional depth is sought across several of the following areas:
Machine learning, deep learning, foundation models, LLMs, training, fine-tuning, inference, quantization, and model evaluation
GPU computing, CUDA, Triton, TensorRT, vLLM, and comparable inference/runtime technologies
Distributed computing, HPC, multi-GPU systems, networking, memory optimization, and performance engineering
Python combined with strong systems-level development experience in Rust, C++, or comparable languages
Linux, containers, Kubernetes, MLOps, observability, and production infrastructure
AWS, Azure, GCP, bare-metal infrastructure, and hybrid or local compute architectures
RAG, embeddings, reranking, vector search, knowledge graphs, document intelligence, and agentic systems
Compiler technologies including LLVM, MLIR, XLA, Triton, or accelerator-oriented compiler stacks
Computer architecture, GPUs, NPUs, tensor accelerators, ASICs, FPGAs, RTL, memory hierarchies, and high-speed interconnects
Semiconductor fabrication, photolithography, EDA, physical design, process engineering, advanced packaging, chiplets, or tape-out
Advanced additive manufacturing, printed electronics, or emerging fabrication methods
Cybersecurity, edge computing, robotics, RF, defense technology, or other technically demanding systems environments

The technical bar is intentionally high, no candidate is expected to possess all listed skills.

The ideal candidate can understand an AI workload at the model level, profile its behavior at the systems level, identify bottlenecks imposed by current computing architectures, and reason downward toward a purpose-built accelerator.

Particular interest exists in people who have crossed traditional disciplinary boundaries: AI engineers who understand silicon, semiconductor engineers who understand machine-learning workloads, HPC engineers who have built sophisticated AI systems, compiler engineers who understand accelerator architecture, hardware engineers with serious software expertise, and researchers capable of turning theory into working systems.

This is fundamentally a builder role
. The CTO must be comfortable operating without a large engineering organization, an established playbook, or layers of abstraction separating leadership from implementation.

Exceptional critical thinking ability, technical independence, curiosity, and the ability to rapidly become competent in unfamiliar disciplines matter as much as any particular technology stack.
